context:
Goal: know whether your tests would catch a broken change.
Problem (rule): no repo measures this on product code, so weak tests pass unseen; your 12:23 CST ruling says a practice joins only when it makes the build better.
Based on (measured): q_max has about 1000 merged pull requests, and banchi and degen hundreds; the lines each one changed are a ready test bed.
Based on (ruling): your Nov 1 12:23 CST ruling: measured value first.
Departs from: main (no such measure on product code) — adds a one-time replay over past merged pull requests.

Your question, "don't these repos have tons of history already?": yes, so the measure can come from history, with no two-week wait.

options.gain: Measured value from history, today, with no load on builders.
options.how: One lane plants small bugs in the lines changed by the last 50 merged pull requests in q_max and banchi, offline, and reports which bugs the tests missed and how many later real bugs those misses pointed at. Then you rule on a merge check.
options.label: Replay the last 50 merged pull requests

options.gain: Weak tests are stopped at once.
options.how: A low score blocks the batch merge from the start.
options.label: Block merges now

title: Should your repos measure whether their tests catch a deliberately broken change?
why: History gives the measure today, and your ruling asks for measured value first.
